prompt: Create an editorial topographic capacity map for a tiny service studio: several independent scheduling layers flow around obstacles and resolve into a few clear openings. Warm off-white surveyor paper, cropped landscape chart. Elegant contour lines, three moss-green terrain ribbons, small vermilion survey pins and blocked zones, subtle unlabeled coordinate grid. Hand-inked cartographic print with screen-printed pigment, precise but tactile, flat archival daylight. Wide 3:2 composition, densest terrain on the right with calmer negative space at upper left, no frame. Palette: parchment, dark teal ink, moss, muted ochre, vermilion. Fine recycled paper grain, crisp engraved linework. Abstract resources only. No people, no UI, no readable words, no calendar icons, no logos, no watermark. Avoid gradients, glossy 3D, neon, generic corporate illustration, illegible pseudo-text, brands, real locations.
review: Accepted first candidate: no text artifacts, brands, people, seams, or misleading UI; palette and composition match thesis.
